fields.description:
Well, after a long time, The Pit Level 3 has been completed.

This hack was started in 2015 and I worked hard on it until mid-2017. For personal reasons, I was forced to interrupt progress and it was practically stopped until 2022. From 2022 onwards I managed to work hard on it again and finish it.

The focus of this hack was not difficulty, although it is somewhat complex. My goal was to make a fun hack. Because it was mostly made between 2015 and 2017, this hack is made up of many shelljumps, yumps, keyjumps and things like that. Nowadays, that's not as cool as it was in 2015, but I didn't have much of a choice. I managed to change many rooms and eliminate some repeated shelljumps, but overall if I were to change everything, I would have to do a new hack.

FULL HACK VIDEO: https://youtu.be/mrlO3VQiz9U

Anyway, that was the most I could do. Although this hack is full of shelljumps/keyjumps, it also has some cool tricks, as you will see in some rooms.

NOTE: The water room (room 112) is different from what appears in the video. I changed it because it was generating a lot of lag, but unfortunately I couldn't change it in the video, as the TAS was desyncing.

NOTE 2: The crash at the end of the video was for pure fun, it is not mandatory. The hack ends as soon as you kill the boss.

That's it, download and enjoy!

fields.description:
You exit from your last-played level victorious. The design was fine, if not familiar, but engaging and fun. You jumped over the pits, you avoided the munchers, and touching the goal tape felt satisfying enough. The gimmicks were really neat, and some of the more unique elements ignited your imagination about the yet unplayed levels that await on the road ahead. What new obstacles would the creator expect you to overcome? As you ponder this, traversing the overworld of the hack you are currently playing, you see a streak of green and yellow flash across the sky. Is it a bird? Is it a plane? No, it’s a caped union plumber indulging in aerodynamic equestrianism! At first they look ridiculous and awkward. It doesn’t even look fun, but, you can’t stop watching. How are they even doing that? It looks hard, but also kind of interesting. Their horse doesn’t even have wings! Why does it keep sticking its tongue out?! You think to yourself, “Could I do it too?” A disembodied voice whispers back into your thoughts, “You can, if you try.”

Chinese astrology says the Year of the Horse is upon us! This first of its kind Yoshi horse flight hack comes as an unlikely collaboration between 4 joint 2006 Time Magazine ‘Person of the Year’ award recipients. The premise is simple, in every level you must eat the 5 golden berries and then hatch and collect your prize. The path to credits has 9 levels, and there are 4 bonus levels after the credits that include 3 guest levels. This hack is not a tutorial. It is a challenge that tests your understanding and consistency of control, and allows you to improve as you go. There is a simple practice level within the hack that provides a space to work on your horse and horseless flight fundamentals freely.

Good luck, and safe flying. We believe in you.

fields.description:
After using my first hack's feedback to gain some semblance of kaizo knowledge, I decided to work on a hack with substantial, hard levels, with a lot more polish.

While one play tester suggested a master rating, the others suggested expert, so it has been submitted as such under the moderator's discretion.

These levels have very long sections, and that's by design, it's what I like. There's 3 kaizo blocks in 25 exits for you to find.

I came in with the goal of better palettes, backgrounds, overall visibility, and less blind setups.

If you have the gumption, this is a much better hack than Nakama, and I would suggest playing this instead.

Some of this hack draws clear inspiration from Super Dram World 3, but well over half of Arcadia was finished before its release. Long sections and survival/stall were the original design ideas in which I started building it.

Enjoy!

fields.description:
Originally submitted as an entry to the Questionable Level Design Contest #3, The Dimensional Castle started as a personal challenge.

How fast I could make a very hard short adventure? And thus, this hack was born.

After the events of Aeron's Golden Cookie Quest and Ganbare Aeron (work in progress, I know...), our goofy magician embarks on a new adventure once again. Many strong foes and traps await Aeron inside The Dimensional Castle. But you're not alone, trustful allies will also be there to give you motivation to keep going further. Can you defeat the source of evil behind the hellish stronghold?

What you can expect from this hack:
- Ruthless foes;
- Tight platforming;
- Questionable level design choices;
- Worldbuilding;
- A E S T H E T I C S ;
- Diverse selection of NPCs;
- A varied bizarre soundtrack;
- Cutscenes;
- Wacky storytelling;
- Jokes;
- Various quality of life changes;
- "Instant" Instant Retry (like the one seen in Boxman Tano);

Compared to the contest version, this one includes additional content, such as:
- Rebalanced level design;
- Unlockable rewards;
- Even more fun NPCs;
- Challenging hidden areas;
- Reworked title screen;
- Expanded intro sequence;

While I'm aware this project has a lot of intentional infuriating design choices and painful moments, inspired mainly by my experiences with Brandish (SNES) and the Castlevania series, I do hope that people can still have fun playing this silly hack of mine.

And this is my questionable experiment! Cheers!

name: A Strongly-Worded Letter to the Iceberg

fields.description:
Welcome to the 21st century in imperial Super Mario World. A rogue paramilitary force known as "ice" has emerged and threatens our collective future (in Super Mario World). Agents of ice seek to infiltrate your neighborhood, sow terror and chaos, and hurt you or those around you (in Super Mario World) and you must not allow yourself to be manipulated into helping them. Your duty to your country (which is Super Mario World) is noncooperation with ice. You owe these bastards less than nothing.

This is what can be loosely described as a gimmick hack where every level has ice physics. This ice is mostly incidental, in that levels would function about the same without it (this is definitely not a metaphor). These levels, while far from my hardest, are spiritually some of my most evil. They can be played in any order, and checkpoints are saved automatically.

This is also a prequel to Trans Liberation; most of the levels are more traditional in comparison but #7 will give you a taste of that sort of gameplay. If you're looking for a realistic gateway into combination long & hard levels, try skipping some checkpoints in this hack.

One extra level can be found through the credits room. It's a 5 room castle but you get a few extra chances near the middle. In my opinion this is the best level in the hack, and I recommend it to anyone who plays a lot of hard hacks or likes to seek out extra challenges. If that doesn't sound like your speed, or it proves too extreme, there's a free play option too. Neither yield an exit.

In the process of making this hack, I have come to love it. I hope you, gentle player, will come to feel the same way.

fields.description:
Dear Explorer,
this once-proud kingdom has fallen long ago, but why? Please help us explore these ruins. Uncover their secrets. Slay the corrupted beasts that plague these lands, and find out what truly happened in the past.

Precision86 Part II : The Forgotten Kingdom is a direct sequel to Precision86, a Kaizo ROMHack that focuses mostly on precision-platforming, new gimmicks and custom bossfights. It is dedicated to Dennsen86.

This ROMHack is full of new, fresh ideas and innovative systems and bossfights, while staying close to the design philosophy of the first game. The full version will still take some time, but I hope you'll enjoy the demo in the meantime!

- reduced HDMA brightness
- replaced HUD toggle with weapon button toggle option
- your attribute of choice is now visible on the overworld
- lots of smaller, quality of life adjustments based on demo feedback
- improved indicators
- bugfixes

Watch a full playthrough here: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=B42Ymk6o03w

fields.description:
What happens when one has too many level ideas to fit in their current projects or in collabs they are participating? The result is this short challenging hack.

The Found Levels featuring Aeron started as a "hodgepodge" collection of levels, which then, turned out into something entirely different. Stuff that wouldn't fit in my upcoming magnum opus, Ganbare Aeron, and other collab projects, that I'm participating, can be found here.

This hack is much harder than anything I ever made so far, so, knowledge about jump control and SMW mechanics is recommended.

The story is set after the events of The Dimensional Castle. Looks like the golden cookie that Aeron retrieved in his previous quests, has been stolen. Equipped with a spatial magic tome, he embarks in a journey, going from one dimension to another, to find it. What surprises await him in this adventure?

Features of this hack:
- Our favorite goofy mage, Aeron;
- A special guest ~omh~ level, but with a twist;
- Seven challenging action stages, one of them being
